summary: WP-P3 adapter-lifecycle trust correction with exactly eight authorized production paths. Preserve six function ports plus one repository-local non-secret store under the same-user/local-workspace trust model. The digest detects corruption/drift, not provenance; authorization exists only when explicit verifyReadiness reaches the active exclusive-write/fsync/rename/owner-and-ACL path after exact WP-P2 verified:true. CLI/MCP errors expose the exact eleven-field whitelist with each value derived from its identically named approved diagnostic except literal-false fallback. runner-owned deliveryStatus remains untouched by Coding.

tasks.title: Add non-secret readiness attestation lifecycle
tasks.objective: Make explicit readiness authorization survive process reconstruction while remaining version-bound and fail-closed.
steps: Document and implement the same-user/local-workspace boundary. The deterministic digest detects corruption and canonical drift only. Reject malformed/extra/tampered/foreign records, target or parent links/reparse points, non-regular files, foreign POSIX owners, permissive POSIX modes, broad/foreign Windows ACLs, and any metadata-command failure.

Create the exact safe schema including authorizationOperation: verifyReadiness. Bind record() through resolved symbols to the active exclusive same-directory wx/0600 writer; complete write, file fsync/close, atomic rename, post-rename owner/file ACL checks, and supported-platform directory fsync. On Windows require an explicit same-directory rename fallback record; never silently omit durability, follow a dead helper, accept append/write, or authorize from presence.

Add the narrow readiness-attestation metadata factory to the existing sole command adapter without changing its credential factory. Bind whoami/icacls plus one fixed non-interactive Get-Acl Owner expression to exact repository directory/file paths; accept no caller path, script, command, flags, environment, stdin, or secret.
Keep six existing function ports unchanged and require the seventh readinessAttestationStore object with record/read/clear/validate.
Clear on the actual init and explicit/automatic backfill paths. After explicit verifyReadiness returns exact verified:true, record the complete safe WP-P2 diagnostics and operation marker.

On query, reject missing/invalid/untrusted evidence before readSemanticReadiness; if trusted, read WP-P2 once only to validate each exact attested version/channel. Clear and reject stale evidence with current safe diagnostics before retrieval.

Trust rationale: a durable local record is required because process memory is not an authorization boundary. The accepted canonical JSON authority already assumes a same-user local workspace, so this design adopts that explicit boundary rather than inventing a signing secret. A malicious process under the same OS identity can rewrite canonical JSON and is out of scope. Other identities, links/reparse points, permissive ACL/mode, corruption, malformed/extra fields, foreign records, and interrupted replacement are in scope and fail closed. The deterministic digest is only corruption/canonical-byte evidence; explicit-verification provenance derives from the guarded verifyReadiness writer path plus OS trust checks.

Windows ownership/ACL evidence requires the eighth narrowly authorized production file systemMetadataCommandAdapter.js because Node fs does not expose Windows ACLs and every other Graph RAG module is prohibited from importing child_process. Its existing credential adapter remains unchanged; a separate exact-path metadata profile is authorized.

Frozen runtime coverage now includes presence-only, malformed, extra, tampered, foreign-workspace, symlink/reparse, independent permissive file ACL, permissive parent-directory ACL, foreign-owner identity, interrupted committed-target and temporary-only, canonical-byte drift, init/backfill/actual MCP mutation invalidation, and independent canonical/content/index/channel drift.

The ninth guard resolves the active record() call graph rather than counting dead atomic calls, enforces file and directory durability including explicit Windows fallback, and checks every error field's same-name diagnostic provenance. Dead-helper append/write and wrong constant/cross-field serializer fixtures are mandatory.
